$comment: Config for the promise plugin, at .claude/promise.config.json. Every field is optional — a project with none of this still gets full detection (see references/config.md). minSkillVersion is the oldest promise skill this project expects: adopt writes the running skill's version, and an older copy warns. docsHome / frameworkPath / plansFolder / commands pin what orient.py would otherwise detect; decisionPolicy is the repo's decision policy (fast, auto or spec; auto when unset), which every new doc takes; branch names the branch arm works on: a pattern with {slug} in it (default feat/{slug}), or current to stay on the branch the session is on, for a host that allows one branch per session; adopt never writes it. protectedPaths names the paths a pull request sized tiny may not touch (changed_rows.py --size tiny). pinFiles names the places besides .claude/settings.json (whose promise marketplace pins a release tag in source.ref) that pin promise, each a path and a pattern whose first group is the value, a commit sha or, with kind version, a version (pin_check.py reads them; upgrade.py moves them, but never a site marked vendored: true alone). upstreamPath names a local promise checkout that reads a private upstream with its own git access. map turns on the bridge to a project's own machine-checked register of promises, and most projects start with no map at all. This file shows every field at once so each one has an example: copy it, then delete whatever this project does not need.

commands.$comment: The verify commands the writing modes run at hand-back through adapter.py verify. Each is an argv line, split and run with no shell. Once this object exists, detection is off for all three; a null or missing key means 'this project has none'. Delete the whole object to go back to detection.

map.$comment: Present only when this project keeps its own capability map — a machine-checked register of promises and the tests that prove them. Start one with scripts/start_map.py, which installs the skill's starter map (templates/starter-map/) and writes this object; examples/minimap/ in the plugin repository runs the same reader over example rows. recipe is the authority for mechanics: read it, do not expect this skill to restate it; whether a row is filed, and how big it is, is the skill's (references/sizing.md). find/row/nextId and checks are argv lines, split and run with no shell (an argument is appended as one argv element) — no pipes, &&, env prefixes or cd; put such logic in a script and name it here. learn is optional: the argv line that records the words find missed a row by, which adapter.py learn runs with --query-file, --row and --source appended (the starter reader's learn); refsSync, also optional, is the one reconcile runs with --input <merged pull requests as JSON> to record which rows each merged pull request named; code, optional too, prints the local files a row's cited tests import (adapter.py code <id>), read before a wide code search. rowIdPattern validates any row id this skill writes or parses. lanes maps the four altitudes (plus sibling) to this project's own evidence-array names, so references/altitude.md can stay generic. checks run, in order, at the end of arm/intake/reconcile and as check.py's checks step; the key is optional, but a project with no checks writes [] — with the key absent, adapter.py checks refuses (exit 2, 'map.checks is not configured'). issueTracker enables a duplicate-issue search before anything gets filed. file names the map's own JSON file, and junit the JUnit XML files or folders this project's test commands write; scripts/check.py joins the two with map_report.py (for the starter map, file can be left out: it is the map.json beside capability_find.py). surfaces is the command that prints the code's entry points, one per line — an argv line or, as here, an argv array — which check.py runs with no shell so the report can list every entry point no row names; requireHomes: true makes check.py fail on a test or an entry point with no row. A map counts as configured only with recipe, find, row and lanes (orient.py's mapUsable). Omit this whole object for a project with no map yet — see references/config.md 'Without a map'.
